title: AI-500: Designing and Implementing Multi-Agent AI Solutions
subtitle: Build a platform of cooperating AI agents on Microsoft Foundry in Python, and prepare for the AI-500 expert exam
description: Most teams run one AI agent. This course teaches you to design and build a whole system of agents, and to run it in production.

You join Larkspur Mutual, an insurer whose claims-intake agent is doing well, until the business asks for more than one agent can carry. Across seventeen modules you follow one company and one claim platform: you design stateful agent loops, coordinate teams of agents, connect them to tools and data, secure and govern them, measure them, control their cost, and handle the night something goes wrong.

A short Larkspur chapter sets up the problem. The concept builds up on screen as a diagram, with the design decision and its trade-offs. Then you see real Python code with the current SDK names. Hands-on lab videos follow, where every step is run on camera, and portal demos show the same ideas in the Azure portal and Microsoft Foundry.

The course is aligned to the skills measured for exam AI-500, which leads to the Microsoft Certified: Multi-Agent AI Solutions Expert certification. Where Microsoft is retiring a feature, you learn its successor, so what you build matches what is current today.
By the end you can design, build, secure, evaluate and operate multi-agent AI solutions on Azure, and you are ready to prepare for the exam with confidence.
outcomes: Design stateful agentic loops with the Responses API, checkpoints, forks and resume
Orchestrate teams of agents with hub-and-spoke, hierarchical and parallel patterns in the Microsoft Agent Framework
Decompose tasks and let agents collaborate and communicate with each other using A2A
Connect agents to tools and data with MCP servers, Azure AI Search retrieval and Azure Cosmos DB memory
Ship agent changes safely with GitHub Actions pipelines, versioning and rollback
Secure agents with zero-trust identity, and govern them with responsible AI controls and lifecycle policies
Trace, evaluate and budget a multi-agent solution, and add human approval where it matters
Prepare for Microsoft exam AI-500 across its skill areas
requirements: Python: you can read and write functions, classes and async code
Basic knowledge of building one AI agent on Microsoft Foundry (for example from exam AI-103 or AI-102 level)
An Azure subscription and a GitHub account to do the labs yourself (some Azure services incur charges)
No data science background is needed
audience: AI engineers and architects who move from building one agent to designing a system of agents
Candidates preparing for Microsoft exam AI-500 and the Multi-Agent AI Solutions Expert certification
Developers who already built an agent and now need state, orchestration, security and operations in production
Platform and DevOps engineers who will run agents for a business
instructor: Microsoft Certified Trainer | Azure and Conversational AI

about.text: Most teams run one AI agent. This course teaches you to design and build a whole system of agents, and to run it in production.

You join Larkspur Mutual, an insurer whose claims-intake agent is doing well, until the business asks for more than one agent can carry. Across seventeen modules you follow one company and one claim platform: you design stateful agent loops, coordinate teams of agents, connect them to tools and data, secure and govern them, measure them, control their cost, and handle the night something goes wrong.

items.label: Design
items.text: stateful agentic loops with checkpoints and resume, orchestration patterns (hub and spoke, hierarchical, parallel), task decomposition and agent collaboration, and agent-to-agent communication with A2A.

items.label: Build
items.text: production prompting for agents, tool ecosystems with MCP, advanced retrieval with Azure AI Search, agent memory in Azure Cosmos DB, and CI/CD with GitHub Actions.

items.label: Secure and govern
items.text: zero-trust security for agents, responsible AI governance, and agent lifecycle governance from first version to retirement.

items.label: Operate
items.text: observability across agents, evaluation of whole claims, staying within budget, human approval in the loop, and incident response at three forty-seven in the morning.

about.text: A short Larkspur chapter sets up the problem. The concept builds up on screen as a diagram, with the design decision and its trade-offs. Then you see real Python code with the current SDK names. Hands-on lab videos follow, where every step is run on camera, and portal demos show the same ideas in the Azure portal and Microsoft Foundry.

about.text: The course is aligned to the skills measured for exam AI-500, which leads to the Microsoft Certified: Multi-Agent AI Solutions Expert certification. Where Microsoft is retiring a feature, you learn its successor, so what you build matches what is current today.
By the end you can design, build, secure, evaluate and operate multi-agent AI solutions on Azure, and you are ready to prepare for the exam with confidence.
